Assistant Benchmark creator David Pawlan sits down with a16z's Anish Acharya to unpack the sudden explosion of personal AI agents and what it will take for one to become part of everyday life.

David has been testing dozens of assistants across real-world tasks, from managing email and booking travel to handling financial admin. They discuss why the most useful agents may become increasingly invisible, proactively checking you into flights, finding refunds, filing reimbursements, or simply handling the small tasks that pile up across everyday life.

They also explore whether the winning interface is an app, text thread, voice, or wearable; how much autonomy consumers will actually give their agents; and what happens when agents start interacting with other agents. From commerce and restaurant reservations to entirely new agent-native services, Anish and David ask what the internet looks like when software starts acting on our behalf.

America’s car affordability crisis is getting worse.

The average price paid for a 3-year-old vehicle in the US surged to a record $32,461 in Q2 2026.

This officially surpasses the previous record of $31,628 set in 2022.

Since 2020, the average price of a 3-year-old vehicle has soared +$9,701, or +43%.

The squeeze is becoming even more visible at the lower end of the market, where a $10,000 to $15,000 budget now buys a vehicle averaging nearly 9 years old with ~98,000 miles.

In 2019, the same budget bought a vehicle less than 5 years old with ~58,000 miles.

Even used car ownership is becoming a luxury.

BREAKING: The delinquency rate on Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) for offices rose +9 basis points in August, to 12.0%, its 2nd-highest reading on record.

This is now only below an all-time high of 12.3% set in January 2026.

The CMBS delinquency rate is now 6 times higher than it was in early-2023.

By comparison, the post-2008 Financial Crisis peak was ~10.8%.

Meanwhile, the overall US CMBS delinquency rate has more than doubled since 2022, to 7.9%, its highest since early 2021.

Excluding the 2020 pandemic, this is the highest delinquency rate in 13 years.

The commercial real estate downturn is intensifying.
